correctness.rationale: The finite Boolean lattice has automorphism group S_n acting on its atoms; stabilizing every individually named subset forces the product of symmetric groups within identical membership columns I_sigma, hence orbit coordinates c_sigma and the binomial class size/product count. Incoming and outgoing cover degrees distinguish ranks after one round. Each atom has (a-1)! upward paths to a uniquely named rank-a marker iff it belongs, allowing the marker bit vector to be separated in at most n-1 rounds. At rank k+1, the sum of the k+1 predecessor count-vectors is k times c(Y), recovering the next rank after one further round, proving the 2n-2 bound. n=1 and empty or zero/full markers are consistent special cases; fixed lattice internal orbit exactness is not global graph identification. An independently written synchronous directed-WL enumeration tested 223 distinct-marker configurations across n=2..5, with maximal observed three rounds. Bounded tests are not the all-n proof.

evidence: Kiefer–McKay study general iteration numbers of colour refinement and extremal graphs with bounds in vertex count, not a rank-linear 2n-2 guarantee for directed Boolean covers carrying arbitrary named markers.
